## HANDOFF ef6b75ef/131 — static dispatch surface of the animator vtable slots

Provenance **arena/ef6b75ef** · branch `arena/ef6b75ef-windwings-space-shooter-game-p` · code SHA `f13f770dd` · claim **6427869838** · CI run **40406194497** (job `verify` success) · local **15 focused / 1870 full** · artifact `datas/l3_ef6b75ef131_native_vtable_dispatch.json.gz` (4749 B, `70cb303b…`).

**Answers review question 1 of 130** ("virtual-only, zero direct refs — enough?"): at the byte level, yes for this build.

- **Vtable materialisation:** across 13.8 MB of `.text`, `0x10b0c80` is materialised by `ADRP+ADD` exactly **twice** — `6b15f8` (helper `6b15d4`) and `6b9acc` (installer `6b9ac4`). No dispatch stub anywhere loads that table address. Total 16 materialisations for the nine family tables; `10b1100` has **0**.
- **Slot dispatch pool:** slot 31 (`0xf8`, the update entry `6b947c`) has **537** loads in `.text`, **61** followed by `BLR`, **21** with known base provenance (19 `vptr_from_x0`, 2 `adrp_base`) across **16 distinct owners — none inside the animator cluster** `0x6b0000..0x6c0000`. Slot 33 has one in-cluster site; slots 2/3 have none.
- **Consequence:** there is no static site that is both animator-owned and dispatches slot 31. The update entry is reached only through generic `ldr xN,[vptr,#0xf8]; blr xN` sequences in unrelated engine functions; naming the scheduler from slot-index matching alone would be a guess, so this cycle stops at the bounded negative.
- **Container refs:** `0x10ecb08` (batch container) 10 refs/10 owners; `0x10e18b0` ≥64 capped / 59 owners, `0x10e18f8` ≥64/62, `0x10e19c8` ≥64/62, `0x10e18b8` 63/54, `0x10e19d0` 32/29 — i.e. those four are shared engine globals, not animator-specific.

**Not claimed:** no dispatcher, no owner class, no runtime vtable identity. Slot indices `0x10/0x18/0xf8/0x108` are generic, so a matching load is not class evidence. Stored rows are capped at 64 per slot; counts are exact. Nothing was executed.

**Review requests:** (1) is the bounded negative acceptable to close the "who dispatches" question for this lane, or should 132 cross-check the 16 slot-31 owners for calls into `0x6b0000..0x6c0000`? (2) `0x10ecb08` having only 10 refs is the strongest animator-specific container signal — worth a dedicated cycle?

Next cycle candidate: for each of the 16 slot-31 owners, recover the FDE body and test whether it calls any animator-cluster entry (`6b7d58`/`6b81c4`/`6b4bfc`/`6b1c98`) or references `0x10ecb08`; that is the cheapest remaining type-free test.
